extracted.intended_audience: federal agency staff, regulated industry, legal counsel, and public stakeholders interested in the creation, content, and procedural treatment of federal agency guidance documents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the procedural, legal, and substantive expectations for federal agency guidance documents and for sector-specific guidances (e.g., FDA device/clinical/testing guidances). Covers how guidance should be drafted, reviewed, published, the non-binding nature of guidance, and substantive recommendations that guidances provide to regulated parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance documents are non-binding/voluntary
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for any requirements specified in the statutes cited in the guidance document, the contents of this guidance document do not have the force and effect of law and do not bind the public in any way. Conformity with any recommendations in this guidance document, as distinct from statutory requirements, is voluntary only, and nonconformity will not affect rights and obligations under existing statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in multiple notices (e.g., State Freight Plans guidance): guidance documents should state their non-binding nature and not be treated as regulations absent statutory incorporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat guidance alone as imposing binding obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies: do not treat those guidance documents alone as imposing binding obligations both in law and in practice, except as incorporated into a contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance should not be used as the sole basis for enforcement or to create legally binding duties unless incorporated by contract or statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take public input into account for significant guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should take public input into account in formulating significant guidance documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant guidances should provide opportunity for comment or otherwise consider stakeholder input when being formulated, per E.O./policy references in the Federal Register excerpts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make guidance documents readily available to the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must make guidance documents readily available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish guidance on accessible websites, provide downloads, and supply copies on request (examples: FDA, DOT posting locations and email request contacts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance documents should receive legal review and appropriate senior review
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures ensure that all guidance documents receive legal review and, when appropriate, Office of the Secretary review. Guidance proposed to be issued by a component must be reviewed and cleared by OGC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal review and clearance (e.g., Office of General Counsel, Office of the Secretary) are required steps before issuance to ensure legal sufficiency and departmental alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance must comply with relevant statutes and regulations (including statutory deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidance document complies with all relevant statutes and regulation (including any statutory deadlines for agency action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drafting and review must verify that guidance does not conflict with existing statutes/regulations and respects statutory timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance documents should identify or include required elements (per agency procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: DOT's review and clearance of guidance shall ensure that each guidance document proposed to be issued by an OA or component of OST satisfies the following requirements: ... (b) The guidance document identifies or includes:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOT (and similar agencies) require guidances to explicitly identify certain elements (the excerpt cuts off, but indicates required content/identification clauses are mandatory under review rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on guidance as separate basis for affirmative enforcement action
rubrics_metrics.description: The contents will not be relied upon by the Department as a separate basis for affirmative enforcement action or other administrative penalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should refrain from using guidance alone to justify enforcement; enforcement should be tied to statutory or regulatory obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance should be consistent with Executive Orders and Departmental Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: This guidance document updates and replaces prior guidance and also updates the guidance to be consistent with recent Executive Orders and DOT Orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When issuing or updating guidance, agencies should harmonize content with relevant executive and departmental policy directives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency may withdraw guidance documents (with effective date)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Transit Administration withdraws guidance document Circular 4703.1, Environmental Justice. The withdrawal is applicable as of [date].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance issuance procedures include mechanisms to rescind or withdraw guidance documents and to announce effective dates for such withdrawals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance should explain agency 'current thinking' and expectations for regulated parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft/final guidances are intended to inform regulated industry about the Agency's current thinking regarding the criteria, process, and expectations for [topic].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency guidances articulate the agency's interpretation and expectations (non-binding) to help regulated entities understand agency review and compliance expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for mandatory cosmetic recalls: criteria, process, and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides answers to common questions about FDA's mandatory recall authority for cosmetics; intended to inform regulated industry about the Agency's current thinking on implementation of certain aspects, including the criteria, process, and expectations, for mandatory recalls of cosmetic products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A guidance on recalls should set out the criteria that trigger recall actions, the procedural steps the agency expects, and what industry should anticipate in implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on FDA records access authority for cosmetics: criteria and process for records access
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides answers to frequently asked questions about certain authorities for FDA to access records related to cosmetic products and informs regulated industry about criteria, process, and expectations for FDA's access to these records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance should explain the statutory/regulatory bases for records access, the scope of information that may be sought, and expectations for industry cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations for non-clinical testing and clinical study design for medical devices with weight-loss indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides recommendations regarding non-clinical testing and clinical study design for medical devices with indications for use associated with weight loss to support premarket submissions; includes discussion of how FDA considers the benefit-risk analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Premarket guidances should recommend appropriate non-clinical tests, clinical trial design elements, endpoints, and how to frame benefit-risk considerations to support submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for using the Plausible Mechanism Framework for individualized therapies
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes considerations for generating substantial evidence of effectiveness and evidence of safety of individualized therapies based on a plausible mechanism framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance should outline evidentiary standards and study design considerations for demonstrating safety/effectiveness when traditional trial approaches are not feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations for information to include in submissions for patient-matched orthopedic implant guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides recommendations regarding information that should be included in regulatory submissions for patient-matched guides for orthopedic implants and recommendations manufacturers should consider when developing their design process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance should list recommended submission content, design controls, and process-documentation expectations to promote clarity and consistency in review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations for testing blood donations for Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides recommendations for testing blood and blood components for HBsAg to reduce the risk of transfusion-transmitted hepatitis B virus; intended to supersede earlier recommendations and memoranda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance should specify recommended testing strategies, sample types, and testing algorithms to mitigate infectious disease transmission in blood products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal study design recommendations for dental bone grafting material device 510(k) submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides recommendations for animal study design and animal study information to include to support a 510(k) submission for dental bone grafting material devices; may help manufacturers comply with special controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance should describe appropriate animal models, endpoints, study durations, and reporting elements that support device safety/effectiveness in premarket notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance testing and labeling recommendations for menstrual products
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides recommendations for performance testing, labeling, and information for inclusion in premarket notification (510(k)) submissions for tampons, pads, and menstrual cups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance should describe test methods, performance criteria, labeling content, and submission materials to promote consistency and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited programs guidance for regenerative medicine therapies
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides sponsors with recommendations on the expedited development and review of regenerative medicine therapies for serious or life-threatening diseases or conditions; will supersede prior guidance when finalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance should define eligibility, data expectations, and procedural steps for expedited pathways; clarify how the agency will evaluate benefit-risk under the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended compliance policy for certain NIOSH-approved air-purifying respirators
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides a proposed compliance policy and information about respirators approved by NIOSH; intended to facilitate more efficient and effective use of resources consistent with least burdensome policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance should clarify which premarket/other requirements apply and explain least-burdensome approaches consistent with public health and regulatory safety objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred loan sizing methodology for transit-oriented development (TOD) projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes a preferred maximum loan sizing methodology that correlates the value of the transportation benefits a TOD project generates with the maximum size of a loan the Bureau would anticipate accepting as a policy matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for credit programs should tie policy metrics (transportation benefits) to underwriting limits and clarify the scope of projects to which the interim policy applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on referrals for potential criminal enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes DoD's plans to address criminally liable regulatory offenses under the executive order on Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance should outline referral thresholds, interagency coordination, and procedures for referring potential criminal regulatory offenses for further action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance availability and access obligations (publication and distribution channels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons interested in obtaining a copy of the guidance may do so by downloading an electronic copy from the internet; guidance documents are available on agency websites, Regulations.gov, and upon email request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance issuance practice should include clear electronic access instructions, document numbers/titles for identification, and alternative distribution methods for those unable to download.
